title: Review: Nuclear structure and notation; Rutherford scattering and atomic models; Charged particles in uniform electric fields; Particle accelerators and detectors
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: Q06-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; Q06-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; F05-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; P04-1#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: F05-1#N.14, N01-1#N.5, P04-1#N.14, Q06-1#N.4, F05-1#N.3, N01-1#N.3, P04-1#N.12, Q06-1#N.7a, F05-1#N.5a, N01-1#N.10, P04-1#N.5, Q06-1#N.14a. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Neutron
items.clue: Particle found with protons in the tiny positive core; discovered in 1932.

items.label: Atom
items.clue: About 10⁻¹⁰ m across: roughly 10⁴ to 10⁵ times wider than its positive core.

items.label: Electron
items.clue: Negative particle pushed against E, with about 1800 times the acceleration of a proton.

items.label: Synchrotron
items.clue: Ring accelerator of fixed radius in which B is raised in step with the particles' momentum.

questions.stem: A proton and an alpha particle are placed, one at a time, at the same point in a uniform electric field. The alpha particle has twice the charge of the proton and about four times its mass. Gravity is negligible. What is the ratio (acceleration of the alpha particle) / (acceleration of the proton)?
questions.explanation: Correct. Acceleration = charge × E ÷ mass, so the ratio is (2/4) = 1/2. The alpha particle accelerates half as much.

questions.stem: Predict first. Carbon-12 (¹²₆C) and carbon-14 (¹⁴₆C) are isotopes of carbon. Which statement about these two nuclides is correct?

options.text: They contain the same number of neutrons but different numbers of protons.
Both contain the same number of protons, but different numbers of neutrons.
Their atoms have different chemical properties, as their nuclei differ.
Their nuclei are identical, but their atoms have different numbers of electrons.

questions.stem: A ring's bending magnets already run at their maximum field. Engineers want protons with three times the momentum. What must they do?

options.text: Build a ring with nine times the bending radius, since kinetic energy goes as momentum squared.
Build a smaller ring, since faster protons are easier to steer.
Build a ring with three times the bending radius.
Keep the ring and add more accelerating cavities.

questions.explanation: Radius = momentum ÷ (B × charge). B cannot rise, so the radius must rise in proportion: three times the momentum, three times the radius.

questions.stem: Predict first. Which statement about the results of the Geiger–Marsden–Rutherford alpha-particle scattering experiment is correct?

options.text: Most of the alpha particles were deflected through large angles, and only a few passed straight through.
Nearly all the alpha particles passed through almost undeflected; a very few were deflected by more than 90°.
The few alpha particles that bounced back had collided with the electrons in the gold atoms.
The few alpha particles that bounced back had struck the hard outer surface of a gold nucleus.

questions.stem: Two horizontal parallel plates, 2.5 cm apart in a vacuum, have a potential difference of 150 V between them. What is the magnitude of the acceleration of an electron between the plates? Gravity is negligible. Take e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and m_e = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg.
A nucleus of potassium-40 is written in nuclear notation as ⁴⁰₁₉K. Which statement about this nucleus is correct?

In a detector with a uniform magnetic field, a V of two tracks starts from one point. Both products have the same size of charge. One track has a much larger radius of curvature than the other. What does this show?

options.text: The particle with the larger radius had more momentum.
The particle with the larger radius had more charge.
The particle with the larger radius was neutral.
The two particles had the same momentum but different masses.

questions.explanation: r = p/BQ. Same B and same size of Q, so the larger radius means the larger p.

questions.stem: A gold nucleus has radius 7.0 × 10⁻¹⁵ m and a gold atom has radius 1.4 × 10⁻¹⁰ m. Roughly what fraction of the atom's volume does the nucleus occupy?
questions.explanation: (7.0 × 10⁻¹⁵ ÷ 1.4 × 10⁻¹⁰)³ = (5.0 × 10⁻⁵)³ = 1.25 × 10⁻¹³. The atom is almost entirely empty space.

questions.stem: Two parallel plates, 2.0 cm apart in a vacuum, have a potential difference of 500 V between them. An electron is released from rest at the negative plate and accelerates across the gap. What is its speed when it reaches the positive plate? Take e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and m_e = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg.
Which pair are isotopes of the same element?
A cyclotron accelerates protons with a fixed magnetic field. It is now used for alpha particles: twice the charge, about four times the mass. What must happen to the frequency of the alternating pd?

options.text: It must be doubled, because the alpha particle has twice the charge.
It can stay the same, because the time per half-turn does not depend on speed.
It must be quartered, because the alpha particle is four times as heavy.

questions.explanation: The frequency is proportional to charge ÷ mass. 2 ÷ 4 = ½, so each half-turn takes twice as long.

questions.stem: A gold nucleus is about 1.4 × 10⁻¹⁴ m across and a gold atom is about 2.9 × 10⁻¹⁰ m across. In a scale drawing the nucleus is a dot 1 mm across. How wide must the atom be drawn?
